decisions.statement: A rule's match does not depend on the rules beside that rule.
Where two rules match one case, which of them acts is the caller's to settle.
Each rule is one page in a folder.
Several rules stating one action are several rules rather than one rule copied.
A rule is carried out by code or by an agent.
A rule's kind does not change how the rule matches.
A code rule states the actions to take.
An agent rule leaves the final action to the agent.
A rule's kind is the folder the rule is in rather than a key on the rule.
The engine answers of one rule whether that rule matches the case at hand.
The engine reads a run of text as one value of a vocabulary of patterns.
The engine carries out no action.
Nothing here reads a rule from disk.
A match is a set of conditions.
Every condition of a match must hold for the match to hold.
A match with no conditions matches everything.
A condition names one property of the page being matched.
A condition names the values that condition accepts.
A condition holds where the property has a value the condition names.
A negated condition holds where the property has no value that condition names.
The ways a condition compares a value are a closed set.
No comparison a condition makes is a regular expression.
Every comparison has a negated spelling.
A condition compares without regard to case.
Nothing proves a rule set to be a partition.
Nothing walks the cases a rule set can tell apart.

definition: what every rule set runs on

directives.name: Ask Before Changing
directives.act: Get approval from the person the rules serve before a change, never after.
directives.warrant: A rule acts on the next thing it matches, so asking after is asking about what is in force.
aids: Being asked to change it is not approval.
Related changes serving one goal are one change.
